subject: Money
title: Transfer Pricing
description: A fast breakdown of Transfer Pricing for builders.

hook.text: Google shifted $23 billion to Bermuda in one year using a method called the Double Irish Dutch Sandwich.

buildup.text: Transfer pricing: a company sells products to its own subsidiary in a low-tax country at inflated prices.

discovery.text: This moves profits to where taxes are lowest. The real work happens in one country; the profit lands elsewhere.

twist.text: It's legal. Tax laws allow companies to set internal prices. The rules were written with their lobbyists' help.

climax.text: Developing countries lose $100 billion yearly to transfer pricing. The poorest nations suffer most.

punchline.text: The profit goes where the tax isn't.

quiz.question: What is transfer pricing?
options: Setting prices between a company and its own subsidiaries
